answer: Because the atlas stake is held until the vertex settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the violet audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 10% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a trivial one. A farm running 66 keys therefore burns that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
